item.title: Behavioural Environmental Economics & Policy (BEEP): trends and reflections
item.content:encoded:
Sanchayan Banerjee, King's College London

Lory Barile, University of Warwick

This special issue focuses on Behavioural Environmental Economics & Policy (BEEP), which examines how departures from rational choice assumptions—such as bounded rationality and bounded willpower—affect environmental decision-making and policy effectiveness. The issue seeks to consolidate evidence on how behavioural insights can improve the design and evaluation of environmental policies to address urgent challenges including climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution.

The special issue welcomes conceptual, empirical, and policy-oriented contributions applying behavioural insights to environmental problems. Submissions may employ various methodologies including experiments, quasi-experimental designs, and literature reviews. The issue particularly values work that identifies both market and behavioural failures, designs and tests policies combining traditional instruments with behavioural tools, and evaluates their effectiveness and welfare impacts.

This is an invitation-only special issue in Environmental and Resource Economics.

Appel publié par Environmental and Resource Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Interactions between market failures and behavioural failures in environmental settings
  • Policy design that combines prices/standards with behavioural tools (defaults, salience/framing, simplification, commitment)
  • Welfare analysis (including psychological costs), ethics, and paternalism in environmental policy
  • Empirical identification of behavioural mechanisms; field/lab/quasi-experimental evidence
  • Heterogeneity, equity, and distributional consequences of behavioural environmental policies
  • Replication, meta-analysis, and open-science practices in this domain
  • Choice architecture and environmental outcomes
  • Interactions between behavioural instruments and prices/regulation
  • Climate cognition and communication
  • Evaluation and methods

Timeline

  • November 30, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: Bounded Rationality
item.content:encoded:
This special issue honors the contributions of Reinhard Selten to the fields of bounded rationality, behavioral economics, and game theory. The issue invites submissions that advance our understanding of how cognitive limitations and bounded rationality shape economic behavior and decision-making.

Contributions are welcome that explore the theoretical foundations and empirical applications of bounded rationality in various economic contexts, including but not limited to individual choice, strategic interaction, market behavior, and organizational decision-making.

Appel publié par Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Bounded rationality and economic behavior
  • Decision-making under uncertainty
  • Behavioral economics
  • Cognitive limitations in economic decision-making
  • Game theory and bounded rationality

Timeline

  • December 31, 2026: Full paper submission deadline

item.title: The evolution of decision-making and reasoning from childhood to adulthood
item.content:encoded:
,

,

This special issue examines how decision-making processes, choice behavior, and reasoning capabilities evolve from childhood through adulthood. Understanding the developmental trajectory of these fundamental cognitive and behavioral processes provides insight into the mechanisms that underlie human judgment and decision-making across the lifespan.

The collection seeks to integrate perspectives from developmental psychology, behavioral economics, cognitive science, and neuroscience to explore how individuals acquire, refine, and modify their decision-making strategies as they mature. Contributions may address the biological, cognitive, social, and environmental factors that shape the development of choice behavior and reasoning abilities.

Empirical studies, theoretical frameworks, and methodological approaches that advance our understanding of developmental decision-making are welcome. This includes research examining both normative development and individual variation in how people learn to make choices and engage in reasoning from early childhood through adulthood.

Appel publié par Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Developmental changes in decision-making and choice behavior across the lifespan
  • Cognitive mechanisms underlying reasoning development
  • Economic decision-making in children and adolescents
  • The role of emotions and affect in developing choice behavior
  • Neural and biological substrates of reasoning development
  • Individual differences in decision-making trajectories
  • The impact of education and experience on choice behavior
  • Temporal and risk preferences across development
  • Social influences on reasoning and decision-making
  • Irrational choice patterns and their developmental origins
